item.title: Hydrotherapy, Relaxation and Wellness
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Hydrotherapy, Relaxation and Wellness

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

At ETE, we design and manufacture hydrotherapy, relaxation and wellness solutions for thermal spas, spas, hotels, thalassotherapy centres and wellness projects that seek to complete their circuit with added-value experiences. We work so that each installation combines comfort, functionality and reliable service, always with equipment adapted to the real use of the centre, which aims to have a stable clientele because regular visits improve their health.

We do not understand these spaces as a sum of isolated products. We study how each area should work, what role it plays within the user journey and what technical needs lie behind it so that the final result makes sense. That is why we develop custom-made solutions, manufactured with technical criteria and designed to last.

 

Solutions to enrich the user experience

In a wellness area, not everything depends on pools, showers or sweating equipment. There are also installations focused on water massage, thermal rest and user comfort before, during and after the circuit. These types of solutions make a difference in the perception of the service and help raise the overall quality of the space.

At ETE, within this line we group equipment that responds to three very specific functions: hydrotherapy treatments with professional intervention, thermal relaxation areas and auxiliary services that improve the centre’s daily operations. We manufacture and integrate them coherently with the rest of the project.

 

Our solutions in hydrotherapy, relaxation and wellness

Within this family, we work with equipment that provides treatment, rest and comfort for the end user. The following stand out among them:

Jet Spray with Oils

We manufacture Jet Spray with Oils equipment for hydro-massage treatments with therapist intervention. It is an automatic solution that produces hot water shocks at 39 ºC and cold water shocks at 8 ºC, with pressure, temperature and cycle control, to perform complete or partial body massages with precise technical application.

It is an installation designed for centres that want to incorporate a high therapeutic and sensory value water treatment. We design the equipment so that the service is stable and adapts to the real dynamics of the thermal spa or spa, integrating hot and cold water production within the whole installation.

Thermal Lounger

At ETE, we also manufacture anatomical thermal loungers for relaxation areas at 38 ºC. They are pieces of equipment designed to promote rest after the water circuit or as part of a wellness area focused on prolonged user comfort.

Our loungers can be installed indoors or outdoors and are heated by water, not by resistance, which allows us to work with a solution that is more coherent with the technical philosophy of the rest of the project. They incorporate an anatomical cushion and each unit has an approximate consumption of 500 W, powered through the heating system defined for the installation.

 

Swimsuit Dryer

The Etedryer Swimsuit Dryer completes the user experience and improves the centre’s operations. It allows swimsuits to be dried in just 10 seconds, without damaging the fabrics, and helps prevent the appearance of mould and bad odours in changing rooms and exit areas.

It is safe, compact and low-noise equipment, with a power of 243 W. It adapts easily to new or existing installations and can include options such as a water collection tank, coin mechanism or custom colour, depending on the needs of the establishment.

We design each project to measure

Each wellness centre has a different logic. There are projects where the Jet Spray must be integrated as a cabin or specific treatment, others where thermal loungers are an essential part of the relaxation area, and others that need to reinforce user service with auxiliary solutions such as the swimsuit dryer. At ETE, we analyse each case to define which equipment fits best and how it should work within the whole.

Our work is not limited to supplying a specific unit. We study the available space, working temperatures, heat or cold production when necessary, intensity of use and integration with the rest of the circuit. This allows us to achieve coherent, profitable installations with a long service life.

Tell us what type of experience you want to offer in your thermal spa or spa. At ETE, we will analyse the space, the intensity of use, the working temperatures and the functions each piece of equipment must cover in order to propose a custom-made solution. Our goal is for the installation to respond well from day one and to improve the health of the clients who visit each week, with long-term stability.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What equipment does this hydrotherapy, relaxation and wellness category include?

We include solutions such as Jet Spray with Oils, Thermal Lounger and Swimsuit Dryer. They are pieces of equipment aimed at improving treatment, rest and user comfort within the spa or thermal spa.

Can you integrate this equipment into a complete wellness project?

Yes. At ETE, we work with these solutions as part of a whole. We study how they should fit into the circuit, what technical needs they have and how they should relate to the rest of the centre’s installations.

Does the Jet Spray with Oils require hot and cold water?

Yes. This treatment works with hot and cold water shocks, so it is essential to correctly define temperature production and control in order to guarantee the planned service.

Can thermal loungers be installed outdoors?

Yes. Our thermal loungers can be placed indoors or outdoors, as long as the project correctly defines the installation conditions and the water heating system.

Can the swimsuit dryer be installed in existing centres?

Yes. The Etedryer swimsuit dryer adapts easily to both new installations and spaces already in operation, making it a practical solution to improve service without major complications.

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

We do not understand these spaces as a sum of isolated products.<\/strong> We study how each area should work, what role it plays within the user journey and what technical needs lie behind it so that the final result makes sense. There are also installations focused on water massage, thermal rest and user comfort before, during and after the circuit. These types of solutions make a difference in the perception of the service and help raise the overall quality of the space.<\/p>

At ETE, within this line we group equipment that responds to three very specific functions: hydrotherapy treatments with professional intervention, thermal relaxation areas and auxiliary services that improve the centre\u2019s daily operations. We manufacture and integrate them coherently with the rest of the project.<\/p>

Within this family, we work with equipment that provides treatment, rest and comfort for the end user. The following stand out among them:<\/p>

Jet Spray with Oils<\/strong><\/p>

We manufacture Jet Spray with Oils equipment for hydro-massage treatments with therapist intervention. It is an automatic solution that produces hot water shocks at 39 \u00baC and cold water shocks at 8 \u00baC, with pressure, temperature and cycle control, to perform complete or partial body massages with precise technical application.<\/p>

It is an installation designed for centres that want to incorporate a high therapeutic and sensory value water treatment. We design the equipment so that the service is stable and adapts to the real dynamics of the thermal spa or spa, integrating hot and cold water production within the whole installation.<\/p>

Thermal Lounger<\/strong><\/p>

At ETE, we also manufacture anatomical thermal loungers for relaxation areas at 38 \u00baC. They are pieces of equipment designed to promote rest after the water circuit or as part of a wellness area focused on prolonged user comfort.<\/p>

Our loungers can be installed indoors or outdoors and are heated by water, not by resistance, which allows us to work with a solution that is more coherent with the technical philosophy of the rest of the project. They incorporate an anatomical cushion and each unit has an approximate consumption of 500 W, powered through the heating system defined for the installation.<\/p>

Each wellness centre has a different logic. There are projects where the Jet Spray must be integrated as a cabin or specific treatment, others where thermal loungers are an essential part of the relaxation area, and others that need to reinforce user service with auxiliary solutions such as the swimsuit dryer. At ETE, we analyse each case to define which equipment fits best and how it should work within the whole.<\/p>

Our work is not limited to supplying a specific unit. We study the available space, working temperatures, heat or cold production when necessary, intensity of use and integration with the rest of the circuit. This allows us to achieve coherent, profitable installations with a long service life.<\/p>

Tell us what type of experience you want to offer in your thermal spa or spa. At ETE, we will analyse the space, the intensity of use, the working temperatures and the functions each piece of equipment must cover in order to propose a custom-made solution. Our goal is for the installation to respond well from day one and to improve the health of the clients who visit each week, with long-term stability.<\/p>

item.title: Thermal Pools and Water Circuits
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Thermal Pools and Water Circuits

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

At ETE, we design and manufacture heating and cooling equipment for custom-made thermal pools and water circuits for thermal spas, spas, hotels, wellness centres and thermalism projects. We study each installation to define the working temperature, the necessary power, the form of heat and cold production and the most suitable technical solution so that the service operates with stability and with reasonable consumption.

Our experience as manufacturers of electric heating equipment since 1977 allows us to approach both the pool and everything behind its operation: water heating, cooling when the circuit requires it, automation, temperature control and adaptation to the centre’s real use. We do not simply supply equipment. We design a complete solution so that the installation performs well from day one.

 

We manufacture water installations designed for the real use of the spa

Each centre needs a different combination of pools, routes and temperatures. Some projects seek a leading hydromassage area, others prioritise relaxation or temperate swimming, deep relaxation pools, and others incorporate water routes to stimulate circulation and enrich the thermal circuit.

That is why at ETE we work on a custom-made basis. We size the power according to the volume of water, the target temperature and the conditions of use, so that the pool or circuit maintains the planned service without oversizing the installation. We can also integrate hot water and cold water within the same technical logic when the project requires thermal contrast.

 

Our solutions in thermal pools and water circuits

Within this line of work, we develop different installations to cover very different functions within the spa or thermal spa. These include the following:

Hydromassage pool 34°C

We manufacture solutions for hydromassage pools at 34°C, a temperature widely used in wellness and thermalism circuits. We design the heating equipment to maintain that temperature with stability and adapt the installation to the volume of the pool, the usage pattern and the type of centre. It is a solution designed to provide comfort, massage and prolonged stay within the route.

Swimming pool 25°C-30°C

We also carry out installations for swimming and exercise pools in approximate ranges from 25°C to 30°C. In these projects, it is essential to correctly calculate the available power, because use, water renewal and heat losses affect the performance of the installation. Our equipment makes it possible to work with temperate temperatures effectively and with a long service life.

Relaxation pool 38°C

We design relaxation pools at 38°C for spaces where the objective is to intensify the feeling of rest and encourage a slower use of the water. In this type of installation, it is essential to guarantee the temperature without fluctuations, since the user’s comfort depends directly on thermal stability. We select the right system so that the pool responds regularly throughout the day.

Deep flotation – Flotarium

We manufacture Flotarium-type flotation pools for thermal spas and spas that seek to incorporate a differentiated experience within their water circuit. This is a specific installation that requires precise technical definition both in heating and in operating conditions in order to preserve its therapeutic and sensory effectiveness. We adapt the project to each centre and develop the heating solution with equipment manufactured by us.

 

Compostela Footbath

The Compostela Footbath is a circuit for walking on rounded pebbles with cycles of hot and cold water that we use to activate circulation and work on reflexotherapy in the feet. We can configure it in different formats and design it to be integrated into the route of the thermal spa or spa. This equipment combines hot water at 40°C and cold water at 8°C, with automation and sprinklers that make it possible to create a controlled contrast experience.

Custom manufacturing for thermal spas, spas and hotels

We work for new projects, extensions and refurbishments. We can intervene in thermal spas, hotel spas, wellness centres, thermal areas and any installation that wants to incorporate hydromassage, relaxation, temperate swimming, flotation pools or water circuits for contrast and wellness.

If you are defining a new water area or want to modernise an existing installation, at ETE we help you select the most suitable solution. We study the dimensions, the desired temperature, the usage times and the logic of the circuit to develop a coherent technical proposal for your project.

Tell us what type of installation you want to develop and what functions it needs to fulfil. At ETE, we will analyse the volume of water, the necessary temperatures, the dynamics of the circuit and the service that each unit must provide in order to propose a custom-made solution. We manufacture according to the real needs of the project, with a technical and practical vision focused on profitability and the long service life of the system.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What types of installations does ETE include within thermal pools and water circuits?

We work with solutions such as hydromassage pool 34°C, swimming pool 25°C-30°C, relaxation pool 38°C, Flotation Flotarium and Compostela Footbath. Each one responds to a specific function within the spa or thermal spa and we design it according to the needs of the project.

Can you manufacture a custom-made thermal pool?

Yes. At ETE, we work on a custom-made basis. We study the volume of water, the target temperature, the frequency of use and the type of centre in order to define the most suitable heating or contrast system.

Do you also calculate the necessary power to maintain the temperature?

Yes. This is one of the key points of our work. We do not only manufacture the equipment; we also calculate the power and temperature needed so that the installation operates with stability and with the fewest possible problems in daily use.

Can you integrate hot water and cold water in the same circuit?

Yes. In many thermalism and wellness projects, it is necessary to combine hot water and cold water to create contrast routes. We can develop the technical logic of the circuit so that both operate in a coordinated way.

Do you only work for large thermal spas?

No. We work both for large thermal spas and spas and for hotels, wellness centres and smaller projects that need a well-sized installation manufactured with technical criteria.

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

item.title: Custom-Made Electric Boilers
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Custom-Made Electric Boilers

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

At ETE, we have been designing and manufacturing custom-made electric boilers since 1977 to respond precisely to every heating need. We do not work with generic solutions when the process requires a specific power, a given temperature or stable service conditions. We study each installation and develop the right electric equipment to produce heat safely, with service continuity and predictable energy consumption.

A custom-made electric boiler makes it possible to adapt the power, type of fluid, voltage, control system and general configuration of the equipment to each client’s real use. This difference is key in industry, in technical installations and in any process where it is not enough to “have heat”, but where it is necessary to have exactly the heat that is needed, when it is needed and with maximum reliability.


Manufacturer of custom-made electric boilers for every process

Each thermal process has its own requirements. Producing hot water for a heating circuit is not the same as generating steam or superheated water for an industrial line, or working with thermal oil at high temperature. That is why at ETE we approach each project from a preliminary study, where we define the power required by the heating process and the type of flow that must carry the heat from the generation point to the consumption point.

Our technicians analyse what needs to be heated, what temperature must be reached, how long the installation needs to respond and what working conditions the equipment will have. With this data, we calculate the exact power and define a custom-made electric boiler capable of guaranteeing the heat service in writing.

This approach makes it possible to avoid two very common mistakes: oversizing the installation or falling short. An oversized boiler increases the investment, the electrical supply and the consumption. A poorly calculated boiler compromises the process and creates instability. Designing to measure means adjusting the solution to real use, not forcing the client to adapt to standard equipment.

The power and flow studies we carry out are exclusively for equipment with ETE technology. If another brand is purchased, the manufacturer must be required to guarantee the heat service and correct operation. In cases where our calculations have been used and another brand has been installed, the equipment has not provided the heat service and there have been process stoppages due to breakdowns.

 

What advantages does a custom-made electric boiler offer?

  • Exact power for the process. Each unit is calculated according to the real heat demand of the installation.
  • Greater service stability. The system works to maintain the necessary thermal input continuously.
  • Simpler integration. The boiler adapts to the electrical and thermal conditions of each project.
  • Predictable energy consumption. The client knows from the beginning what performance can be expected from the equipment.
  • Long service life. A well-calculated solution works with fewer deviations and offers greater long-term reliability.

In ETE’s philosophy, manufacturing to measure does not mean making the project more complicated, but solving it better. The goal is for the equipment to deliver stable heat for years, minimising breakdowns, reducing maintenance needs and providing a solid technical basis so that the installation works as it should.

 

Why choose ETE for a custom-made electric boiler

ETE – Thermic Electric Solutions has been designing and manufacturing custom-made electric heating equipment since 1977. That experience translates into a very specific way of working: study, calculate, manufacture and guarantee.

Our clients are looking for more than an electric boiler. They need a safe, profitable and stable solution for their process. That is why we focus on the robustness of the equipment, the simplicity of maintenance, the predictability of consumption and service continuity.

If you need a custom-made electric boiler for industry, heating or hot water production, at ETE we help you define the most suitable power and configuration for your project. We analyse your real heating need and manufacture equipment prepared to respond reliably from the first day.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What is a custom-made electric boiler?

It is equipment designed based on the real needs of an installation. Instead of choosing a standard model, the power, working temperature and system configuration are calculated so that the heat service adapts exactly to the process.

What applications can a custom-made electric boiler be manufactured for?

It can be developed for hot water, superheated water, steam, thermal oil, heating, DHW and different industrial or technical processes where controlled and continuous heat is required.

What information does ETE need to calculate the equipment?

Mainly, what needs to be heated, what temperature must be reached, what heat service is required, under what conditions the installation will operate and what electrical characteristics the project has.

What advantage does it offer compared with a standard boiler?

The main advantage is real adjustment to the process. A custom-made solution avoids sizing errors, improves service stability and helps ensure that the investment and consumption correspond to the real thermal demand.

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

Our technicians analyse what needs to be heated, what temperature must be reached, how long the installation needs to respond and what working conditions the equipment will have. With this data, we calculate the exact power<\/strong> and define a custom-made electric boiler<\/strong> capable of guaranteeing the heat service<\/strong> in writing.<\/p>

This approach makes it possible to avoid two very common mistakes: oversizing the installation or falling short. An oversized boiler increases the investment, the electrical supply and the consumption. A poorly calculated boiler compromises the process and creates instability. Designing to measure means adjusting the solution to real use, not forcing the client to adapt to standard equipment.<\/p>

The power and flow studies we carry out are exclusively for equipment with ETE technology. If another brand is purchased, the manufacturer must be required to guarantee the heat service and correct operation. In cases where our calculations have been used and another brand has been installed, the equipment has not provided the heat service and there have been process stoppages due to breakdowns.<\/p>

item.title: Success Stories
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Success Stories

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

In the field of industrial heat, trust is built by proving that a solution works in the plant, responds steadily to the demands of the process and delivers measurable results in terms of reliability, control and efficiency. That is why success stories have a special value: they make it possible to see how a technology performs in real situations and what impact it can have on production.

At ETE, we have been developing industrial electric heating solutions for a wide range of applications since 1977. Over these decades, we have worked with companies that needed to solve complex challenges related to heat generation, process stability, the electrification of installations and the replacement of combustion systems with more efficient alternatives.


More than projects, solutions adapted to each process

Every success story starts from a specific need. In some projects, the main objective has been to improve the thermal control of the process. In others, to reduce energy uncertainties, eliminate direct emissions in the plant or adapt an installation to new production requirements. We have also developed solutions for clients who needed safe, custom-made equipment capable of being integrated into industrial environments with very specific requirements.

What all these projects have in common is the technical approach with which they are addressed. At ETE, we do not start from a standard solution and then try to make it fit. We analyse each application, study the real operating conditions and design the thermal system according to the final use, the level of demand and the client’s energy objectives.

 

Experience applied to new industrial challenges

The experience accumulated by ETE across multiple projects is an advantage for companies looking to implement thermal solutions with complete safety. Having worked on diverse applications allows us to anticipate needs, detect critical variables and propose more accurate configurations from the earliest stages of the project.

This practical knowledge is especially valuable when the client is looking for more than just equipment: they are looking for a reliable solution, consistent with their process and ready to evolve with the plant. That is why success stories are not only a sample of work carried out, but also a way of demonstrating how we work.

A starting point for your next project

If your company is studying an industrial heating installation, an electrification strategy or an improvement in the thermal performance of the process, reviewing success stories can help you better understand what solution you need and what results you can expect. At ETE, we put this experience at the service of every new project, with a technical, realistic and performance-oriented approach.

Every process has its own particularities, but experience shows that when the solution is well planned from the beginning, results arrive with greater safety, efficiency and operational continuity.

In these 50 years of activity, we have studied and designed thousands of units for industrial processes, nuclear power plants, petrochemical plants, the food industry, the plastics industry, pharmaceutical companies, hotels, hospitals and centralised heating systems in industries and homes. Today, the enquiries we receive about different heat processes have already been studied, and we have supplied equipment that works for decades without shutdowns or maintenance.

Our work is based on two concepts: engineering work to design and calculate the equipment for each case, and the technology to manufacture the equipment. If you have received a proposal from us, you must install our technology; otherwise, you will have problems with the heat service in your processes.

 

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

item.title: How to Choose the Right Boiler
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
How to Choose the Right Boiler

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

Choosing an industrial boiler should not be reduced to comparing power ratings or reviewing a technical data sheet. In real production environments, the choice of thermal equipment determines the stability of the process, energy consumption, maintenance, safety and the growth capacity of the installation. That is why, at ETE, we approach each project from a complete technical perspective, studying the real use of heat, control needs and the operating context of each client.

Since 1977, we have designed and manufactured industrial electric heating solutions adapted to demanding processes. This experience has allowed us to confirm that there is no single valid answer for every industry. The right boiler is the one that responds precisely to the working conditions of a specific plant, not the one that simply reaches a certain temperature or pressure.

 

What to analyse before selecting an industrial boiler

Before choosing a thermal generator, it is essential to define exactly what the process needs. The first point is to understand the required thermal fluid. Not all industrial processes work with the same heat transfer medium. Depending on the target temperature, the required stability and the characteristics of the process, it may be more suitable to work with steam, superheated water or thermal oil.

It is also essential to determine the real thermal load. Many installations operate with approximate estimates or excessive safety margins that end up generating oversizing. An industrial boiler that is too large can cause unnecessary starts and stops, lower efficiency and a higher investment cost than necessary. In contrast, correctly sized equipment makes it possible to adjust consumption, better control thermal production and extend the service life of the system.

Another key aspect is the way in which heat is demanded. A continuous process is not the same as a cyclical one, nor is a plant with concentrated load peaks the same as an installation with stable consumption throughout the day. The behaviour of the process determines the type of regulation, the advisable thermal inertia and the equipment control strategy.

 

Factors that influence the choice of equipment

When selecting an industrial boiler, it is advisable to assess a series of variables that have a direct impact on the performance and integration of the system:

  • Required working temperature and pressure for the process.
  • Necessary useful power under real production conditions.
  • Most suitable type of thermal fluid.
  • Operating hours and daily demand profile.
  • Available space in the plant and installation constraints.
  • Desired level of automation and monitoring.
  • Safety, maintenance and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • The company’s energy strategy, including electrification and decarbonisation.

At ETE, we do not work with generic solutions. We analyse these parameters to propose robust, reliable and custom-made electric equipment, aligned with the client’s real needs and with the installation’s energy objectives.

 

The importance of working with a specialised manufacturer

When a company considers how to choose the right boiler, it does not only need a catalogue. It needs technical support, experience in industrial applications and real personalisation capacity. That is precisely the difference between selecting a standard product and developing a solution adapted to the process.

At ETE, we manufacture industrial electric boilers and thermal systems designed to respond with reliability, efficiency and control. We study each application, validate the working conditions and guarantee predictable equipment behaviour, including consumption figures defined in writing when the project requires it.

Every industrial installation has its own thermal logic. That is why choosing the right boiler requires a deep understanding of the process, not just the equipment. If your company is evaluating a new installation, a technological replacement or a heat electrification project, at ETE we can help you define the most suitable solution from a technical, energy and operational point of view.

 

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

Choosing an industrial boiler<\/strong> should not be reduced to comparing power ratings or reviewing a technical data sheet. In real production environments, the choice of thermal equipment determines the stability of the process<\/strong>, energy consumption<\/strong>, maintenance, safety and the growth capacity of the installation. That is why, at ETE, we approach each project from a complete technical perspective, studying the real use of heat, control needs and the operating context of each client.<\/p>

Since 1977, we have designed and manufactured industrial electric heating solutions<\/strong> adapted to demanding processes. This experience has allowed us to confirm that there is no single valid answer for every industry. The right boiler is the one that responds precisely to the working conditions of a specific plant, not the one that simply reaches a certain temperature or pressure.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"0684d61","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"What to analyse before selecting an industrial boiler","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"2f36a18","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Before choosing a thermal generator, it is essential to define exactly what the process needs. The first point is to understand the required thermal fluid<\/strong>. Not all industrial processes work with the same heat transfer medium. Depending on the target temperature, the required stability and the characteristics of the process, it may be more suitable to work with steam<\/strong>, superheated water<\/strong> or thermal oil<\/strong>.<\/p>

It is also essential to determine the real thermal load<\/strong>. Many installations operate with approximate estimates or excessive safety margins that end up generating oversizing. An industrial boiler that is too large<\/strong> can cause unnecessary starts and stops, lower efficiency and a higher investment cost than necessary. In contrast, correctly sized equipment makes it possible to adjust consumption, better control thermal production and extend the service life of the system.<\/p>

Another key aspect is the way in which heat is demanded. A continuous process<\/strong> is not the same as a cyclical one, nor is a plant with concentrated load peaks the same as an installation with stable consumption throughout the day. The behaviour of the process determines the type of regulation, the advisable thermal inertia and the equipment control strategy.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":""}],"isInner":""},{"id":"b6a6d51","elType":"section","settings":{"jet_parallax_layout_list":[],"structure":"22","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"3396335"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"7473dfe"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"d16ec32"}],"gap":"wider"},"elements":[{"id":"8568beb","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":66,"_inline_size":65.363,"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f149f54"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"05209c5"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"0e17e60"}],"padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":true}},"elements":[{"id":"18e1b29","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Factors that influence the choice of equipment","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"5eacbb6","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

When selecting an industrial boiler, it is advisable to assess a series of variables that have a direct impact on the performance and integration of the system:<\/p>

  • Required working temperature and pressure<\/strong> for the process.<\/li>
  • Necessary useful power<\/strong> under real production conditions.<\/li>
  • Most suitable type of thermal fluid<\/strong>.<\/li>
  • Operating hours<\/strong> and daily demand profile.<\/li>
  • Available space in the plant<\/strong> and installation constraints.<\/li>
  • Desired level of automation and monitoring<\/strong>.<\/li>
  • Safety, maintenance and applicable regulatory requirements<\/strong>.<\/li>
  • The company\u2019s energy strategy<\/strong>, including electrification and decarbonisation.<\/li><\/ul>

    At ETE, we do not work with generic solutions. We analyse these parameters to propose robust, reliable and custom-made electric equipment<\/strong>, aligned with the client\u2019s real needs and with the installation\u2019s energy objectives.<\/p>

item.title: Efficiency and Decarbonisation
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Efficiency and Decarbonisation

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

Energy efficiency and decarbonisation have become two strategic priorities for industry. It is no longer just a matter of reducing operating costs, but of adapting production processes to a context in which emissions, electrification and the responsible use of energy are part of business competitiveness.

In this scenario, industrial heat plays a central role. Many installations still depend on combustion-based systems to cover their thermal needs, despite the fact that there are alternatives capable of offering more precise control, cleaner operation and a more coherent integration with today’s sustainability objectives.

At ETE, we have been developing industrial electric heating solutions for decades, designed to respond to this transformation. We manufacture robust, custom-made equipment focused on improving the thermal performance of processes, with a clear premise: replacing combustion wherever electric heat can provide a more efficient technical solution aligned with decarbonisation.

 

Energy efficiency in industrial thermal processes

Talking about efficiency in a thermal installation is not only about consuming less. It means using energy in a precise, stable way adapted to the real demand of the process. An efficient system is one that generates the necessary heat at the right time, with the least possible waste and with regulation capable of maintaining performance without unnecessary deviations.

In many industrial processes, efficiency is penalised by oversizing, thermal losses, excessive inertia or poorly adjusted control systems. That is why the design of the equipment and its integration into the plant are just as important as the technology used. At ETE, we carry out an engineering study to define the equipment our clients need and then manufacture the equipment with safe technology resulting from many years of experience.

Industrial electric heating solutions make it possible to move forward in this direction thanks to their response capacity, modulation precision and the absence of losses associated with combustion.

When the system is well designed, thermal energy is generated in a more direct and controllable way, which makes it easier to optimise the process and reduce operational uncertainties. Using ETE heat production equipment makes it possible to eliminate large combustion thermal plants and install a unit next to each thermal consumption point.

 

Decarbonising is not just changing energy source

Industrial decarbonisation is often associated with replacing fossil fuels with electrical or renewable sources. But real change goes further. It involves reviewing how heat is produced, how it is distributed, how it is controlled and how it is integrated into the company’s production logic.

Electrifying a thermal process does not mean exactly replicating a previous solution with another energy source.

It requires redesigning the system to take advantage of electric heat production technology: precision, cleanliness, operational simplicity and the possibility of aligning with long-term energy strategies. At ETE, you will speak with technicians who have experience in producing heat with electricity and will be able to discuss how to change your installations and modernise them so that the processes are safe and reliable.

In this sense, well-planned decarbonisation can provide benefits that go beyond reducing direct emissions. It also improves energy traceability, reduces certain maintenance costs and enables more stable and automated operation. In the future, you will be able to supply electricity to ETE electric thermal equipment with your own renewable energy installations.

 

Preparing industry for the next step

The energy transformation of industry cannot be built with generic solutions. It requires technical knowledge, adaptability and a deep understanding of the process. If your company is evaluating how to improve the efficiency of its thermal system or how to move forward in the decarbonisation of industrial heat, at ETE we can help you study the feasibility and design a solution adapted to your needs.

 

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

Energy efficiency<\/strong> and decarbonisation<\/strong> have become two strategic priorities for industry. It is no longer just a matter of reducing operating costs, but of adapting production processes to a context in which emissions, electrification and the responsible use of energy are part of business competitiveness<\/strong>.<\/p>

In this scenario, industrial heat plays a central role. Many installations still depend on combustion-based systems to cover their thermal needs, despite the fact that there are alternatives capable of offering more precise control<\/strong>, cleaner operation<\/strong> and a more coherent integration with today\u2019s sustainability objectives.<\/p>

At ETE, we have been developing industrial electric heating solutions<\/strong> for decades, designed to respond to this transformation. We manufacture robust, custom-made equipment focused on improving the thermal performance of processes, with a clear premise: replacing combustion<\/strong> wherever electric heat can provide a more efficient technical solution aligned with decarbonisation.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"0684d61","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Energy efficiency in industrial thermal processes","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"2f36a18","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Talking about efficiency in a thermal installation is not only about consuming less. It means using energy in a precise, stable way adapted to the real demand of the process<\/strong>. An efficient system is one that generates the necessary heat at the right time, with the least possible waste and with regulation capable of maintaining performance without unnecessary deviations.<\/p>

In many industrial processes, efficiency is penalised by oversizing, thermal losses, excessive inertia or poorly adjusted control systems<\/strong>. That is why the design of the equipment and its integration into the plant are just as important as the technology used. At ETE, we carry out an engineering study to define the equipment our clients need and then manufacture the equipment with safe technology resulting from many years of experience.<\/strong><\/p>

Industrial electric heating<\/strong> solutions make it possible to move forward in this direction thanks to their response capacity, modulation precision and the absence of losses associated with combustion.<\/p>

When the system is well designed, thermal energy is generated in a more direct and controllable way, which makes it easier to optimise the process and reduce operational uncertainties. Using ETE heat production equipment makes it possible to eliminate large combustion thermal plants and install a unit next to each thermal consumption point.<\/strong><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":""}],"isInner":""},{"id":"b6a6d51","elType":"section","settings":{"jet_parallax_layout_list":[],"structure":"22","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"3396335"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"7473dfe"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"d16ec32"}]},"elements":[{"id":"8568beb","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":66,"_inline_size":65.363,"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f149f54"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"05209c5"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"0e17e60"}],"padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":true}},"elements":[{"id":"18e1b29","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Decarbonising is not just changing energy source","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"5eacbb6","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Industrial decarbonisation<\/strong> is often associated with replacing fossil fuels with electrical or renewable sources. But real change goes further. It involves reviewing how heat is produced, how it is distributed, how it is controlled and how it is integrated into the company\u2019s production logic.<\/p>

Electrifying a thermal process does not mean exactly replicating a previous solution with another energy source.<\/p>

It requires redesigning the system to take advantage of electric heat production technology<\/strong>: precision, cleanliness, operational simplicity and the possibility of aligning with long-term energy strategies. At ETE, you will speak with technicians who have experience in producing heat with electricity and will be able to discuss how to change your installations and modernise them so that the processes are safe and reliable.<\/strong><\/p>

In this sense, well-planned decarbonisation can provide benefits that go beyond reducing direct emissions. It also improves energy traceability<\/strong>, reduces certain maintenance costs and enables more stable and automated operation. In the future, you will be able to supply electricity to ETE electric thermal equipment with your own renewable energy installations.<\/strong><\/p>

item.title: What Power Does Your Process Need?
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
What Power Does Your Process Need?

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

Determining what power an industrial process needs is one of the most important decisions when designing a thermal installation. It is not only about reaching a specific temperature, but about ensuring that the system can maintain the required performance with stability, efficiency and safety under real working conditions. An incorrect calculation can lead to productivity losses, unnecessary consumption or operational limitations from the very first day.

At ETE, we have been developing industrial electric heating solutions adapted to each application since 1977. Our experience has shown us that power sizing should not be based on generic approximations, but on a rigorous technical analysis of the process, operating times and the real thermal behaviour of the installation.

 

Why an approximate estimate is not enough?

In many industrial plants, thermal power is calculated by applying wide margins “just in case”. Although this practice aims to avoid falling short, in practice it often leads to oversizing that penalises investment, makes regulation more difficult and increases energy consumption. The opposite can also happen: equipment that appears sufficient on paper, but in production does not achieve the necessary response and creates bottlenecks.

Calculating power correctly means adapting the system to the effective demand of the process. This means knowing precisely how much heat is needed, how quickly it must be supplied and with what level of continuity or modulation the equipment must operate.

Our calculations are applicable exclusively for the use of our equipment and technology. In our experience, when equipment from other brands has been installed using our calculations, the installation has had many problems.

 

Variables that determine the necessary power

The power of an electric heating unit depends on several factors that must be analysed together. Among the most relevant are:

• The fluid to be heated and its thermal properties.

• The initial temperature and the target temperature.

• The flow rate or volume of product or fluid that needs to be heated.

• The time available to reach the required temperature.

• The thermal losses of the installation.

• The type of process: continuous, discontinuous, batch-based or with demand peaks.

• The environmental conditions and the insulation of the system.

• The reasonable safety margin according to the criticality and variability of the process.

With ETE technology for producing heat, we recommend dispensing with large combustion boilers and many metres of pipe networks. We recommend installing an ETE electric heating unit in each heat process, avoiding heat losses in networks that can exceed 30% of the total process.

Each of these variables directly influences the useful power that the equipment must deliver. That is why, in industrial applications, it is not advisable to rely on generic tables without validating the real operating context.

 

A solid basis for more efficient processes

Correctly sizing the thermal power is a strategic decision. It affects process performance, energy cost, installation reliability and the possibility of moving towards more efficient and decarbonised models. With a well-planned calculation, the company gains control, reduces uncertainty and has a more solid technical basis to grow or transform its production.

If your company needs to define the thermal power of a new process, replace an existing installation or evaluate an industrial electric heating solution, at ETE we can help you study the case and develop the most efficient and safe alternative.

 

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

Determining what power an industrial process needs<\/strong> is one of the most important decisions when designing a thermal installation. It is not only about reaching a specific temperature, but about ensuring that the system can maintain the required performance with stability, efficiency and safety<\/strong> under real working conditions. An incorrect calculation can lead to productivity losses, unnecessary consumption or operational limitations from the very first day.<\/p>

At ETE, we have been developing industrial electric heating solutions<\/strong> adapted to each application since 1977. Our experience has shown us that power sizing<\/strong> should not be based on generic approximations, but on a rigorous technical analysis of the process, operating times and the real thermal behaviour of the installation.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"0684d61","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Why an approximate estimate is not enough?","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"2f36a18","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

In many industrial plants, thermal power is calculated by applying wide margins \u201cjust in case\u201d. Although this practice aims to avoid falling short, in practice it often leads to oversizing<\/strong> that penalises investment, makes regulation more difficult and increases energy consumption. The opposite can also happen: equipment that appears sufficient on paper, but in production does not achieve the necessary response and creates bottlenecks.<\/p>

Calculating power correctly means adapting the system to the effective demand of the process<\/strong>. This means knowing precisely how much heat is needed, how quickly it must be supplied and with what level of continuity or modulation the equipment must operate.<\/p>

Our calculations are applicable exclusively for the use of our equipment and technology. In our experience, when equipment from other brands has been installed using our calculations, the installation has had many problems.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":""}],"isInner":""},{"id":"b6a6d51","elType":"section","settings":{"jet_parallax_layout_list":[],"structure":"22","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"3396335"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"7473dfe"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"d16ec32"}]},"elements":[{"id":"8568beb","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":66,"_inline_size":65.363,"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f149f54"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"05209c5"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"0e17e60"}],"padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":true}},"elements":[{"id":"18e1b29","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Variables that determine the necessary power","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"5eacbb6","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

The power of an electric heating unit<\/strong> depends on several factors that must be analysed together. Among the most relevant are:<\/p>

\u2022 The fluid to be heated<\/strong> and its thermal properties.<\/p>

\u2022 The initial temperature<\/strong> and the target temperature<\/strong>.<\/p>

\u2022 The flow rate or volume<\/strong> of product or fluid that needs to be heated.<\/p>

\u2022 The time available<\/strong> to reach the required temperature.<\/p>

\u2022 The thermal losses<\/strong> of the installation.<\/p>

\u2022 The type of process: continuous, discontinuous, batch-based or with demand peaks.<\/p>

\u2022 The environmental conditions and the insulation of the system.<\/p>

\u2022 The reasonable safety margin according to the criticality and variability of the process.<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false},{"id":"0238a60","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":33,"_inline_size":33.969000000000001,"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"04312df"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"2b03a16"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"e3445f7"}]},"elements":[{"id":"b3f6a75","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/ete.es\/wp-content\/uploads\/2024\/01\/Racional-Peugot-.jpg","id":9477,"size":"","alt":"Racional-Peugot-","source":"library"},"_margin_mobile":{"unit":"px","top":"10","right":"10","bottom":"10","left":"10","isLinked":true}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false},{"id":"266a2f5","elType":"section","settings":{"jet_parallax_layout_list":[],"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"bd7585d"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"33f2593"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"d86147b"}]},"elements":[{"id":"ed6b6e8","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":100,"_inline_size":null,"raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"ed63767"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"28c6558"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"a7c9dea"}]},"elements":[{"id":"d0f0866","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

With ETE technology for producing heat, we recommend dispensing with large combustion boilers and many metres of pipe networks. We recommend installing an ETE electric heating unit in each heat process, avoiding heat losses in networks that can exceed 30% of the total process.<\/p>

Each of these variables directly influences the useful power<\/strong> that the equipment must deliver. That is why, in industrial applications, it is not advisable to rely on generic tables without validating the real operating context.<\/p>

item.title: Steam vs Superheated Water vs Thermal Oil
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Steam vs Superheated Water vs Thermal Oil

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

Choosing between steam, superheated water and thermal oil is a key decision in the design of any industrial thermal system. Each of these fluids has different properties, determines the type of installation required and offers specific advantages depending on the working temperature, the type of process and the level of control required.

At ETE, we design and manufacture industrial electric heating solutions adapted to each client’s specific application. That is why, rather than presenting a generic comparison, we analyse which heat transfer medium is the most suitable for each process, taking into account both the thermal performance and safety, maintenance and operational efficiency.

 

When it is advisable to work with steam

Steam has historically been one of the most widely used thermal fluids in industry. Its ability to transport energy and release heat quickly makes it a common solution in processes where heat transfer, indirect heating or integration with equipment already designed to work with this medium is required.

However, working with steam also involves treating the water, managing condensate, purges and associated maintenance that must be properly resolved in order to maintain system efficiency.

In projects where a steam network already exists or where the process requires this technology due to its characteristics, it may still be a valid option. Even so, it is advisable to study whether it is really the most efficient medium or whether other alternatives can offer more precise control or simpler operation.

 

What superheated water contributes to industrial processes

Superheated water makes it possible to work at high temperatures while keeping the fluid in liquid phase through the use of pressure. It is a very interesting solution when efficient heat transfer, stable heat distribution and more controlled circuit management are required.

Compared with steam, superheated water can offer advantages in certain applications due to its stability and the reduction of certain complexities associated with condensate generation and recovery.

In addition, it is suitable for installations where uniform heat distribution in closed circuits and a high degree of temperature control are required. Heat exchangers, coils or jackets achieve higher performance when using superheated water; there is no need to treat the water and there are no corrosion problems.

Its suitability depends on the target temperature, the plant configuration and the nature of the process. That is why it is important to study not only the thermal working point, but also the dynamic behaviour of the installation and its regulation needs.

 

Thermal oil, an alternative for high temperatures

Thermal oil is a widely used solution when the process needs high temperatures up to 350ºC without resorting to pressures as high as those required by other fluids. Its main value lies in the fact that it allows stable operation in high thermal ranges, which makes it a common option in certain continuous industrial applications.

In return, it requires proper management of the circuit, the condition of the fluid and the associated maintenance.

The behaviour of thermal oil depends on its quality and its degradation over time. Electric thermal fluid heating equipment is designed not to alter the quality of the thermal oil and to avoid the risks of self-ignition. That is why, although it is a very valid technology in certain scenarios, the equipment design must be selected with technical criteria and with a clear view of the installation’s life cycle. ETE’s technicians have extensive experience in the engineering of thermal oil installations and will advise you on the use of this equipment.

 

Defining the thermal fluid correctly improves the entire system

Choosing between steam, superheated water and thermal oil is a decision that affects the performance, safety, efficiency and scalability of the installation. It is not only a technical matter, but also a lever for optimising the process as a whole.

If your company is considering a new thermal installation or reviewing its current one, at ETE we can help you compare alternatives and define the solution that best responds to your production and energy needs.

 

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

Choosing between steam<\/strong>, superheated water<\/strong> and thermal oil<\/strong> is a key decision in the design of any industrial thermal system. Each of these fluids has different properties, determines the type of installation required and offers specific advantages depending on the working temperature<\/strong>, the type of process<\/strong> and the level of control required<\/strong>.<\/p>

At ETE, we design and manufacture industrial electric heating solutions<\/strong> adapted to each client\u2019s specific application. That is why, rather than presenting a generic comparison, we analyse which heat transfer medium is the most suitable for each process, taking into account both the thermal performance<\/strong> and safety, maintenance and operational efficiency.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""},"_padding_tablet":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":"1"},"align_mobile":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"0684d61","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"When it is advisable to work with steam","title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_typography_text_transform":"uppercase","title_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"28","sizes":[]},"title_align_mobile":"center","raven_animated_gradient_color_list":[{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F6AD1F","_id":"f346298"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#F7496A","_id":"8e8923b"},{"raven_animated_gradient_color":"#565AD8","_id":"08e3ded"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"raven-heading"},{"id":"2f36a18","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Steam<\/strong> has historically been one of the most widely used thermal fluids in industry. Its ability to transport energy and release heat quickly makes it a common solution in processes where heat transfer<\/strong>, indirect heating or integration with equipment already designed to work with this medium is required.<\/p>

However, working with steam also involves treating the water<\/strong>, managing condensate, purges<\/strong> and associated maintenance<\/strong> that must be properly resolved in order to maintain system efficiency.<\/p>

In projects where a steam network already exists or where the process requires this technology due to its characteristics, it may still be a valid option. Even so, it is advisable to study whether it is really the most efficient medium or whether other alternatives can offer more precise control<\/strong> or simpler operation.<\/p>

Superheated water<\/strong> makes it possible to work at high temperatures while keeping the fluid in liquid phase through the use of pressure. It is a very interesting solution when efficient heat transfer<\/strong>, stable heat distribution and more controlled circuit management are required.<\/p>

Compared with steam, superheated water can offer advantages in certain applications due to its stability and the reduction of certain complexities associated with condensate generation and recovery.<\/p>

In addition, it is suitable for installations where uniform heat distribution<\/strong> in closed circuits and a high degree of temperature control are required. Heat exchangers, coils or jackets achieve higher performance when using superheated water<\/strong>; there is no need to treat the water and there are no corrosion problems.<\/p>

Its suitability depends on the target temperature, the plant configuration and the nature of the process. That is why it is important to study not only the thermal working point, but also the dynamic behaviour of the installation and its regulation needs.<\/p>

Thermal oil<\/strong> is a widely used solution when the process needs high temperatures<\/strong> up to 350\u00baC without resorting to pressures as high as those required by other fluids. Its main value lies in the fact that it allows stable operation in high thermal ranges, which makes it a common option in certain continuous industrial applications.<\/p>

In return, it requires proper management of the circuit, the condition of the fluid and the associated maintenance.<\/p>

The behaviour of thermal oil depends on its quality and its degradation over time<\/strong>. Electric thermal fluid heating equipment is designed not to alter the quality of the thermal oil and to avoid the risks of self-ignition. That is why, although it is a very valid technology in certain scenarios, the equipment design<\/strong> must be selected with technical criteria<\/strong> and with a clear view of the installation\u2019s life cycle. ETE\u2019s technicians have extensive experience in the engineering of thermal oil installations and will advise you on the use of this equipment.<\/p>

item.title: Climate Control for Hot Yoga and Bikram Rooms
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Climate Control for Hot Yoga and Bikram Rooms

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

At ETE, we design climate control for Hot Yoga rooms with a very clear objective: to achieve a stable, uniform and prepared room so that every class takes place under the right conditions. In this type of centre, it is not enough to heat the environment. It is necessary to control how the heat is distributed, how the humidity responds and how the room behaves when it is full of students exercising.

We work on every installation custom-made because climate control is the core of the Hot Yoga experience. A well-resolved room conveys quality from the very first minute. A poorly climate-controlled room creates cold areas, heat accumulation on the ceiling, unbalanced humidity and an uncomfortable feeling that the student perceives immediately and stops attending classes.

 

Temperature and humidity control with technical criteria

In our line for Hot Yoga, we propose equipment capable of maintaining reference values of around 40 ºC and humidity close to 50%, regulating these parameters according to the centre’s real needs. The key is not to reach a temperature peak, but to sustain a balanced environment throughout the whole class, without sudden fluctuations and without penalising energy consumption.

To achieve this, we study the dimensions of the room, the insulation, the air volume, the number of users per session, the frequency of classes and the way in which the heat must be supplied and distributed. This preliminary work is what allows the climate control to respond precisely and not depend on continuous corrections once the centre is already open.

 

Hot Yoga climate control is not conventional climate control

Hot Yoga rooms have very different requirements from other comfort spaces. Here, it is necessary to work with high temperatures and controlled humidity, while also maintaining a homogeneous feeling at practice level. If the hot air accumulates at the top and the useful area of the room does not reach the same stability, the class loses quality even if the thermometer shows an apparently correct figure.

That is why at ETE we do not approach these projects as standard climate control. We calculate equipment and power according to the specific use of the centre, seeking a stable response, rapid recovery between classes and coherent integration with the ventilation and the rest of the studio’s services.

 

At ETE, we design climate control intended to provide service

We do not just sell a machine. We design a solution so that your Hot Yoga room works every day with stable temperature, controlled humidity and more efficient operation of the centre. When the climate control is well resolved, the user notices it, the studio team works with greater safety and the business gains consistency.

We have studied Hot Yoga centres that close due to lack of students and the problem is that the systems they install to create the ideal climate do not work and students stop attending. We have also seen that they have very high energy costs. The centres that have our technology and engineering are very profitable because many students attend all classes and they have very low energy costs.

If you need to climate-control a new Hot Yoga room or improve an existing installation, at ETE we will study your project to offer you a custom-made solution, with service guarantee and a technical basis designed to last.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Can we climate-control an existing Hot Yoga room?

Yes. At ETE, we study both new openings and rooms already in operation that need to improve uniformity, stability or energy consumption.

What parameters do we seek to control in the room?

We seek to maintain a high temperature and balanced humidity, with homogeneous distribution of the environment and a stable response throughout the whole class.

Why is conventional climate control not suitable?

Because a Hot Yoga room works with very specific temperature, humidity and occupancy requirements. A standard solution usually generates imbalances, cold areas or unnecessary consumption peaks.

Do we advise on the installation?

Yes. Our technicians advise on the installation and provide diagrams and instructions so that the project is carried out with technical criteria.

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD

item.title: Showers and Hot Water for Hot Yoga and Bikram
item.dc:creator: morgan-admin
item.content:encoded:
Showers and Hot Water for Hot Yoga and Bikram

REQUEST YOUR QUOTE

At ETE, we design showers and hot water systems for Hot Yoga with the same technical requirements that we apply to the exercise room. For us, the centre experience does not end when the class finishes. The user also expects a comfortable, stable and well-resolved shower service, capable of responding to several consecutive uses without failures or uncontrolled consumption.

That is why we study each project according to the number of showers, the rotation of students, the frequency of classes and the real demand for hot water. Our goal is for the changing room to operate continuously and for the centre to be able to offer a professional service without depending on oversized or unreliable solutions.

 

Domestic hot water calculated for the centre’s real use

In a Hot Yoga studio, hot water consumption does not behave as it does in a domestic installation. Here, there are very marked demand peaks, especially when several showers are used almost simultaneously after each class. If the system is not properly calculated, service interruptions, waiting times or unnecessary energy costs appear. With our designs and equipment, we achieve savings of 70% in the purchase of equipment and in water and energy consumption.

At ETE, we design equipment to provide hot water for showers with a logic of low consumption and service guarantee. We study the necessary power and the form of integration so that the centre has DHW in a stable way, adapting the solution to the expected intensity of use and to the real size of the changing room.

 

Showers that improve the service and help control consumption

In addition to hot water production, we can integrate timed electronic showers and control solutions that make it possible to better organise water use inside the centre. This type of installation helps to maintain a more constant service, avoids unnecessary consumption and provides a more carefully resolved technical image in the changing room.

When the project requires it, we also incorporate equipment to cool the water and offer cold recovery or contrast showers. This possibility adds value to the service and fits especially well in centres that want to differentiate their user experience beyond the class.

What we solve in the shower area

• Production of domestic hot water for showers with optimised consumption.

• Stable response at times of high demand.

• Integration of timed showers for more efficient use.

• Possibility of cold contrast water according to the centre’s approach.

• Technical advice for hydraulic and electrical installation.

At ETE, we study each project personally

We can size the showers and hot water system for a new opening, a refurbishment or an improvement to an existing centre. We start from specific data and propose a solution adapted to the studio’s pace of use, without improvisations or oversizing.

If you need to ensure hot water, control consumption and offer a better shower service in your Hot Yoga centre, at ETE we will study your project to design a custom-made solution, reliable and ready to work every day.

 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Can we size the hot water according to the number of showers?

Yes. At ETE, we calculate the solution based on the number of showers, the rotation of students, the frequency of classes and the centre’s real demand.

Do we install only hot water or also timed showers?

We can integrate both hot water production and timed electronic showers and other control elements to improve the service and optimise consumption.

Is it possible to add cold contrast water?

Yes. When the project requires it, we can incorporate solutions to cool the water and complete the student experience with cold recovery or contrast showers.

Do we also work on centres that are already open?

Yes. We study refurbishments and improvements to existing installations to resolve service failures, optimise consumption or better adapt the system to the centre’s real use.

SUCCESSFUL INSTALLATIONS ALL OVER THE WORLD
